findings.message: chart.type bar departs from the procedure, which gives arrow (the two series are two periods (2019, 2025) of each category: the change between them is the point (06 DP6-3, G1.46): the default is an arrow chart, each category's change in units and in % side by side (G1.47), or a chart of the change itself (the % panel alone, facts.message relative_change; or the change as bars, a previous_period comparison with transform deviation); clustered bars of the two periods only where each period's own values, not the change, are what the request needs: facts.message periods, with the reason, grounded in the request, in reasons["facts.message"])
findings.title: two periods: an arrow chart

findings.message: the two series are two periods (2019, 2025): drawn side by side they show each category's two values with nothing to suggest change and no change in % (the book's most common mistake, R6-14; G1.46, G1.47)
findings.supply: for the change, the default: x the two periods (kind time, values [2019, 2025] on their grid) with a series per category, type auto (an arrow chart, the change in units and in %); or the change alone as bars (data.comparisons, kind previous_period, the 2019 values, with transform deviation, relative for %); or, where each period's own values are what the request needs, facts.message periods with the reason in reasons["facts.message"]
findings.title: change between two periods: an absolute panel always with a % panel, never clustered bars
